fact: Kayode Adeniyi says a consultancy team on the Central Bank of Nigeria's Anchor Borrowers' Programme in 2021 was using satellite information and GeoAI with farmers.

fact: UNCTAD says Nigeria, with NASRDA as lead partner, has used the CropWatch cloud system since 2021 for crop condition, acreage and yield assessments and pest and drought early warnings.
UNCTAD says CropWatch work in Nigeria feeds a quarterly bulletin informing government policy, with the January to April 2024 bulletin reporting rainfall 64% below the 15-year norm.

Punch reports that NASRDA launched Crop Watch in Abuja, a satellite-based agricultural monitoring system using remote sensing and ground data to evaluate crop growth and yield, with UNCTAD and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
NASRDA states that it produces Nigeria CropWatch crop-monitoring bulletins from satellite data with AIRCAS, under a 4 July 2022 MoU, and mails them to federal ministries, departments and agencies.
NASRDA shows bimonthly CropWatch bulletins for October 2025 and February 2026, disseminated to institutions through a mail list.

NASRDA reports the launch in Abuja of an EU-funded, ESA-implemented Earth Observation-based Agricultural Innovations Project with NASRDA, which will use satellite imagery to monitor crops, land cover and predict yields.

Data Science Nigeria says the Gates-funded Edo State Data Governance platform includes an NDVI and geospatial mapping component giving satellite-driven agricultural monitoring and land-use insights to the state Ministry of Agriculture (subnational, Edo State).
system: Edo Data Governance platform (NDVI geospatial component)

fact: Punch reports the Presidency began field operations of the National Agro-Productivity System pilot in Jigawa State, using satellite imagery every five days and machine learning to track crops, with five-day monitoring due to start around January 2027.
Ecofin Agency reports that Nigeria's space agency NASRDA launched CropWatch in 2024, a crop monitoring system that uses satellite data.

On 17 July 2026 a Nigerian government delegation signed an MoU with OCP Africa and Ground Truth Analytics to launch the National Agro-Productivity System, a satellite and AI crop monitoring platform using images updated every five days, to start with a pilot in one state.

The Federal Government and the EU inaugurated a 2.7 million pound, three-year Earth Observation agricultural project run by NASRDA and the European Space Agency, with demonstration farms in seven states and an open-source agricultural information system to be built integrating satellite data and ground sensors.

NASRDA says it is the national link partner in the Irrigation Earth Observation (IrrEO) project, whose irrigation area mapping tool is developed and funded by stakeholders, and opened a three-day Abuja workshop on mapping irrigated croplands by satellite.

NASRDA's Nigeria customised CropWatch platform, built with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' AIRCAS under an MoU of 4 July 2022, offers NDVI, biomass, VCI, temperature and precipitation deliverables downloadable at national, state and local government level, though NASRDA says other components are still to be completed.
NASRDA says it has participated in publishing the quarterly CropWatch bulletin on crop production including Nigeria since the last quarter of 2021, with 7 editions to the date of the workshop.
